EXTEND C0004 | FIND: `scan_health()` only inserts keys into `tools_available` for tools whose runner returns or throws; if `source_paths` contains no existing files it returns `HealthScan(elapsed_s=...)` with an empty `tools_available` map, and even on non-empty scans missing tools are omitted rather than explicitly marked unavailable unless an exception escapes the runner. Evidence: early return `if not existing: return HealthScan(...)`; runners currently swallow NOT_FOUND and return `[]`, so availability is under-specified at the report interface. FOLLOW: downstream consumers cannot distinguish “no scan run / file set empty” from “all tools healthy but found nothing”, and any UI or brain logic reading `tools_available.get(tool)` must treat absence ambiguously. This compounds the existing availability bug by making report state non-total. FIX: initialise `tools_available` with all expected tool names set to `False`, then overwrite per tool with actual availability status from runner execution.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually test the patched file in project context; it copies only the target file to a tempdir and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that isolated file path. For import-dependent modules, this changes analyzer behaviour materially: sibling imports, package-relative imports, config discovery, and repo-level pyright/ruff settings are no longer resolved as in the real source tree. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`; no package tree or config files are copied; post-fix analysis runs `_count_tool_issues(..., patched_path)` against the lone file.
FOLLOW: fix evaluation verdicts can be silently wrong in both directions. A harmful fix may be marked SAFE because breakage in imports or package integration is invisible in the one-file sandbox; a good fix may be marked HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE because relative imports fail only in isolation. This crosses the immune pipeline interface: `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` marks findings `verified=True` when endocrine returns SAFE/NEUTRAL, so false SAFE results can prematurely close bugs and suppress further review.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — sandbox the file within a copied project subtree instead of as a lone basename: copy the full source root (or at minimum the target file’s package directory plus relevant config files), apply the patch at the same relative path, and run tools from that sandbox root against the relative target path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71
DESCRIPTION: FIND — test execution in `evaluate_fix()` usually does not exercise the patched code. The patched file is written into `tmpdir`, but `test_cmd` is executed unchanged: `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`. In the actual caller from `immune_agents.py`, the command is `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`. With only one patched file in `tmpdir`, pytest resolves `bench/tests/` from the original repo or fails to find tests, and imports during tests resolve against the real source tree, not the patched file in tempdir.
FOLLOW: `tests_passed=True` can be assigned even when the proposed fix breaks the target module, because the tests are running against unmodified code. Since `_compute_fix_verdict()` treats passing tests plus unchanged counts as SAFE, the endocrine layer can certify bad fixes as verified. That directly feeds the immune bug-closure path (`verified=True`), producing silently wrong closure decisions in the distributed review.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when sandboxing, run tests against a sandboxed project tree and rewrite/construct `test_cmd` so its paths target that sandbox; simplest sufficient form is to copy the repo subtree needed for tests into `tmpdir` and execute the same relative pytest command there after patching the corresponding file in that tree.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` uses only the sum of net tool deltas: `total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`; it marks a fix HARMFUL only if `total_net > 0`, SAFE if `total_net < 0`. This lets regressions in one dimension be cancelled by improvements in another. Example from the code path: a fix that introduces 1 new bandit issue and removes 2 ruff warnings yields `total_net = -1` and is classified SAFE.
FOLLOW: harmful fixes with new security/type errors can be misclassified as SAFE/NEUTRAL whenever they also reduce unrelated lint noise. That is silently wrong output, not polish, and it directly affects `immune_agents` Stage 4 where SAFE/NEUTRAL marks a finding verified and closes the bug. Cross-category cancellation defeats the stated contract “no new issues introduced”.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive per-tool delta (`net_type_errors > 0` or `net_ruff_errors > 0` or `net_bandit_issues > 0`) as HARMFUL, and only use reductions to distinguish SAFE from NEUTRAL when no category regressed.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can patch the wrong file because it matches on substring containment: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A filename fragment extracted from description/fix such as `brain.py` or `endocrine.py` can match multiple paths; the function returns the first match without disambiguation.
FOLLOW: fix evaluation may modify and analyse a different file than the finding refers to. The downstream consequence is a fabricated verdict: SAFE/HARMFUL is attached to `finding_id` for the wrong source file, which can verify or reject a fix unrelated to the actual bug. In a multi-module bench this is especially likely where names recur across packages.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — require an unambiguous path match: first prefer exact normalized path or exact basename among `source_paths`; if multiple matches remain, return `None` and mark the evaluation UNEVALUABLE instead of picking the first substring hit.
VERIFIED: TRUE

CONFIRM C0021 — tool timeout handling is missing in runners; `run_pyright`/`run_ruff`/`run_bandit`/`run_mypy` only special-case `NOT_FOUND`, so timeout outputs flow into parse paths and are treated as ordinary empty diagnostics or parse warnings.

CONFIRM C0029 — `run_pyright()` parses only `result.stdout`; if pyright emits JSON on stderr on some failure/error paths, diagnostics are lost because stderr is ignored except for exact `NOT_FOUND`.

EXTEND C0005 | FIND: the dead/partial feature surface also includes fix-evaluation sandboxing as advertised versus actual behaviour. The module docstring promises “sandboxed (tempdir, never modifies actual source)”, but current implementation only isolates writes, not analysis context or tests, so the feature fires but does not validate the real patched program. FOLLOW: this is not just completeness drift; it creates false verification signals consumed by `immune_agents` to mark bugs closed. FIX: narrow the advertised capability to “single-file isolated smoke check” or implement project-tree sandboxing so the claimed feature is true.

CONFIRM C0003 — declared categories `OFF_BY_ONE` and `RACE_CONDITION` are unreachable from current categorisers; no code path emits them.
